newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble dips as funds come from T-bill market.
newsitem.headline: Rouble dips as funds come from T-bill market.

text.p: The rouble eased in lively trading on Thursday as funds flowed into the currency market from the government bond market, dealers said.
"The dollar edged up earlier and is standing at the upper level of the central bank's rates... It is difficult to find any other source of the rouble inflow but Treasury bills," one dealer said.
Wednesday's auctions of bonds and bills were oversubscribed, leaving disappointed bidders looking for a home for their funds.
TOKObank dealer Alexei Golovenko said rates were unlikely to move for the rest of the day, unless banks needed roubles for specific purposes.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,446-49 per dollar compared with an early 5,444-47 and 5,438-40 late on Wednesday. Tomorrow roubles eased to 5,448-50 per dollar from yesterday's late 5,444-46.
The central bank said it had set 5,439-5,449 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Thursday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 5-15 percent, the same as late on Wednesday.
